title: CUDA error: out of memory
body: I successfully installed vLLM in WSL2, but initializing the sample with a local facebook_opt-125m model fails while allocating the CPU cache with `RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory`. The log reports 37375 GPU blocks and 7281 CPU blocks. I am using Python 3.10.11 on Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS under WSL2 with an RTX 3090 24GB.

symptoms_visible: Initializing vLLM with my local OPT-125M model in WSL2 reaches cache initialization and then throws `RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory` from `allocate_cpu_cache`.
The initialization log reports 37375 GPU blocks and 7281 CPU blocks even though the model is only OPT-125M.
N0.label: N0 small model fails during cache initialization

symptoms_visible: With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and `gpu_memory_utilization=0.50`, initialization still throws the same CUDA out-of-memory error from CPU cache allocation.
The changed run reports 19899 GPU blocks and 7281 CPU blocks.
N1.label: N1 memory-utilization probe reproduces OOM

symptoms_visible: vLLM still fails during cache initialization, while text-generation-webui can load and run `facebook/opt-125m` on the same machine.
N2.label: N2 model works outside vLLM

symptoms_visible: Nothing else is using my GPU before the run; when vLLM tries to load the model, the GPU and VRAM graphs briefly spike and then initialization crashes.
N3.label: N3 competing GPU use ruled out

symptoms_visible: After pair-debugging the WSL2-specific cache-allocation problem, I accepted the temporary source workaround and closed the issue.
N_terminal.label: terminal workaround accepted

question_patterns: Can you retry with a lower `gpu_memory_utilization` and set `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, then paste the resulting error?
Does reducing the requested GPU-memory utilization change where initialization fails?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I set `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and used `gpu_memory_utilization=0.50`, but the error is the same. It still ends at `allocate_cpu_cache` with `RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: At `gpu_memory_utilization=0.50`, the model initializes and generates output normally.
The same OOM occurs at 0.60 instead of 0.50, with a correspondingly different GPU-block count.

edges.comment: Opening response c0 and reporter result c1, on the original reporter's WSL2 system. This is a handler-initiated configuration and diagnostic probe, so it is clarification-only even though lowering utilization was suggested as a possible workaround.

question_patterns: Can you check whether `facebook/opt-125m` loads through another inference path on this machine?
Does the same OPT-125M model run outside vLLM?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, I can load `facebook/opt-125m` with text-generation-webui and get it working.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, the model also runs out of memory in text-generation-webui and standard Transformers.
It works outside vLLM from the Hugging Face model name rather than my local model directory.

edges.comment: Participant1's model-control request in c2 and the original reporter's answer in c4. The answer establishes only that the small model works through text-generation-webui; it does not identify the vLLM failure mechanism.

question_patterns: Can you check whether any other process is using GPU memory before starting vLLM?
What does GPU-memory usage look like immediately before and during initialization?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm pretty sure no other process is using my GPU. The GPU 3D and VRAM graphs are quiet beforehand, then both show a burst while the code tries to load the model.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Another process is already holding almost all 24GB of VRAM before vLLM starts.
The brief utilization spike is slightly taller when I run the script from a different terminal.

edges.comment: Maintainer question c6 and original reporter evidence c9. The remote screenshot is not in the supplied local attachment list, so no image path is referenced. Similar reports from other users are not substituted for the reporter's own evidence.

solution.intent: Treat the misleading CUDA OOM as a WSL pinned-host-memory limitation during vLLM CPU-cache allocation, and temporarily disable pinned memory for that allocation.
solution.concrete_example: In vLLM's `worker/cache_engine.py`, remove or comment out `pin_memory=True` from the `torch.empty` calls that allocate the CPU cache, then rerun the OPT-125M sample. This falls back to non-pinned host memory and avoids WSL's limited pinned-memory capacity.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the WSL environment, stack location, unchanged result at lower utilization, successful non-vLLM load, and lack of competing GPU use. Identifying WSL's pinned-host-memory cap—and explaining why it surfaces as a CUDA OOM during CPU-cache allocation—came from the maintainer's pair-debugging, not from a user-run diagnostic that already named the cause.

edges.comment: Resolution chain c12-c14 on the original reporter's environment: participant1 pair-debugged with the reporter, localized the failure to pinned CPU-cache allocation under WSL, and prescribed commenting out `pin_memory=True`; the reporter thanked the maintainer and closed the issue. The thread does not contain a separately pasted clean rerun, so the graph records acceptance and closure without inventing generated output. Later Linux, larger-model, context-length, quantization, and container reports are separate configurations and are deliberately excluded.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause for the opening reporter: WSL limits pinned host memory, and vLLM's pinned CPU-cache allocation triggers the misleading CUDA out-of-memory error.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the failure is in CPU-cache allocation, OPT-125M works outside vLLM, lowering `gpu_memory_utilization` to 0.50 leaves the same error, and no other process is occupying the GPU.
Must recommend disabling or removing `pin_memory=True` for the CPU-cache allocation as the temporary workaround, rather than treating the 125M model itself as too large.
Must not present lowering `gpu_memory_utilization` or setting `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` as the resolution; both were tried in the reporter's case and the same OOM remained.

Must ask the reporter to rerun after changing the cache allocation before claiming a successful clean run; the thread establishes reporter acceptance and closure but does not contain a separately posted generation result.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical Python user who can install vLLM in WSL2, edit a sample script, set environment variables, change constructor arguments, inspect GPU graphs, and participate in pair-debugging, but relies on maintainers for framework internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite and concise; responds with code and raw trace output, answers direct checks, and closes the issue after accepting the maintainer's workaround.
